question: What are the three elements of a voice signal, and what order do they go in?

body.text: Give them in this order: (1) function and direction, (2) distance and/or speed, (3) function and the stop command. Every voice signal needs all three.
Each voice signal must contain the following three elements, given in the following order: function (such as hoist, boom, etc.), direction; distance and/or speed; function, stop command.

question: Can I give the direction or distance first, before naming the function?

body.text: No. The order is fixed. Function and direction come first, then distance and/or speed, then the function and stop command. Don't lead with the distance or speed, and don't put the direction ahead of the function.

question: Do we have to review voice signals again every day or before every lift?

body.text: This section sets no daily or per-lift repeat. After the signals are agreed on, the workers need to meet again about them only if a worker is added or substituted, there is confusion, or a signal is going to change.
